title: Maplewood's Medicaid spending on orthotic procedures jumps 21.4% in 2024
text:
Maplewood’s Medicaid spending on orthotic procedures jumps 21.4% in 2024
I. F. Cooper
In 2024, Medicaid providers in Maplewood billed $90,959 for services categorized under Orthotic Procedures and services, data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database show. This marked a 21.4% rise compared to 2023, when claim amounts for these services totaled $74,951.
Medicaid is a state-administered public health insurance initiative funded by both federal and state governments. It provides coverage for eligible low-income individuals, seniors, children, and people with disabilities, ranking among the country’s largest health care programs.
Fluctuations in Medicaid billing reflect how taxpayer funds for public health care are distributed within a community.
The Orthotic Procedures and services category includes a defined group of Medicaid services grouped by care type, utilizing standardized HCPCS and CPT code sets. For this data, each billing code was mapped to a single service type using uniform code prefixes and ranges, which allows services to be tracked together without overlap and enables accurate year-over-year comparison and ranking.
Despite an overall increase in Medicaid spending across several categories, Orthotic Procedures and services ranked 13th in Maplewood based on total Medicaid payments for 2024.
Statewide in Minnesota, Orthotic Procedures and services placed 17th for total Medicaid spending during 2024.
Over the five years ending in 2024, Medicaid payments for Orthotic Procedures and services in Maplewood rose by $90,959, reflecting no percentage change over the period. Growth was more pronounced during certain years, notably in 2022 and 2023.
Although billed throughout Maplewood, Medicaid payments in the Orthotic Procedures and services category were mainly concentrated within a small number of ZIP codes. In 2024, ZIP code 55109 saw the most claims, totaling $90,958—making up 100% of Medicaid payments for this service category in the city that year.
Spending within the Orthotic Procedures and services group was also focused among just a handful of billing codes.
To compare, the 21.4% increase in Medicaid payments for the Orthotic Procedures and services category in Maplewood between 2024 and 2023 outpaced the 2.7% rise across all Medicaid categories locally during that time.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reports that combined federal and state Medicaid expenditures reached about $871.7 billion for fiscal year 2023, which made up around 18% of total national health outlays—up steeply from roughly $613.5 billion in 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.
This rise represents an increase of about 40% over a few years, attributed in part to higher enrollment and greater usage during and following the pandemic.
Recent federal legislation during the Trump administration has included sizable plans to scale back Medicaid funding and retool the program. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” which became law in 2025, is estimated to trim over $1 trillion in federal Medicaid funding over the next decade. The measure also introduces requirements such as work mandates and greater cost-sharing, policies that may reduce coverage and funding for certain groups. These adjustments are anticipated to increase states’ financial responsibility for Medicaid and restrict federal funding growth even as the program continues to serve millions across the U.S.
